content.title: About
content.content: Green bean casserole is a classic American side dish made with canned green beans, a creamy mushroom sauce, and crispy fried onions. It is especially popular during holiday meals such as Thanksgiving.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The dish was created in the 1950s after Campbell’s introduced a ready‑made mushroom sauce.
The original recipe uses a fried onion topping that is added at the end of baking for crunch.
Green bean casserole is considered an iconic part of the American fall table.
Variations include adding cheese, bacon, or nuts for extra flavor.
It scales easily, making it a favorite for large gatherings.

items.title: Rich in vegetables
items.content: Green beans provide vitamins A, C, K, folate, and dietary fiber that support digestive health.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: A typical serving contains about 150‑200 kcal, making it a moderately low‑calorie side.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Phytonutrients in the beans help combat oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports heart health
items.content: Fiber and potassium contribute to healthy blood pressure.

items.title: Source of plant protein
items.content: Green beans add a modest amount of protein, useful for vegetarians.

items.title: Mushroom allergy
items.content: The mushroom sauce can trigger reactions in people allergic to mushrooms.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Prepared sauce often contains a lot of salt; low‑sodium versions are recommended.

items.title: Added sugar in canned beans
items.content: Some canned beans have added sugars; choose unsweetened varieties.

items.title: Digestive discomfort
items.content: High fiber may cause gas or bloating in sensitive individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the casserole hot as a side dish or part of a main course. Bake until the onion topping is golden, or reheat in the microwave. It pairs well with turkey, chicken, or as a vegetarian centerpiece.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze up to 2 months; reheat to an internal temperature of 75 °C before serving.
